epilogue: Italy was unifying; the Tsar was freeing Russian serfs the same year.

title: Emancipation Proclamation
prompt: An American president issues a wartime order declaring enslaved people in rebel states to be free, transforming the Civil War into a war against slavery.
hint: A US president issues an executive order freeing enslaved people in Confederate states.
epilogue: Prussia was rising in Europe; Manet was painting scandalous works in Paris.

title: Slavery abolished in the United States
prompt: A constitutional amendment ends slavery in America; days later the president who championed it is shot.
hint: An amendment ends slavery; the president who championed it is assassinated.
epilogue: Brazil still enslaved people; the Second Industrial Revolution was just beginning.

title: Mendel publishes laws of heredity
prompt: An Augustinian friar in a Moravian monastery presents the results of eight years of pea plant experiments to a local natural history society — to almost complete silence.
hint: His work was ignored for 35 years. When rediscovered in 1900, it became the foundation of modern genetics.
epilogue: As Mendel quietly revolutionised biology in Brno, the American Civil War had just ended, and the Meiji Restoration in Japan was only three years away.

title: Meiji Restoration
prompt: A teenage emperor is restored to power as Japan begins a breakneck modernisation.
hint: A young Japanese emperor ends the age of shoguns and opens Japan to modernisation.
epilogue: The US had just survived its Civil War; the Suez Canal was under construction.

title: Suez Canal opens
prompt: A French-led project links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, cutting the journey from Europe to Asia by weeks.
hint: A new canal in Egypt shortens the sea route to Asia.
epilogue: The US completed its transcontinental railroad the same year.

title: Mendeleev arranges the periodic table
prompt: A Russian chemist dreams of a table where all known elements fall into place by atomic weight — and leaves gaps, predicting elements not yet discovered.
hint: He predicted the existence of gallium, scandium, and germanium years before they were found, and his predictions proved correct.
epilogue: While Mendeleev organised the building blocks of matter in St. Petersburg, the Suez Canal opened connecting the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, and the transcontinental railroad was completed in America.

title: German Empire proclaimed
prompt: In the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, the Prussian king is proclaimed German Emperor after defeating France.
hint: A new empire is proclaimed in a defeated enemy's most opulent palace.
epilogue: The Paris Commune rose and fell the same year; Japan was abolishing the feudal domain system.

title: Japan forces Korea to open
prompt: Japanese warships force Korea to sign a treaty opening its ports — mirroring what America did to Japan twenty years earlier.
hint: Japan uses gunboat diplomacy to force Korea open, as America had done to Japan.
epilogue: The Battle of Little Bighorn happened the same year; Alexander Graham Bell was patenting the telephone.

title: Bell patents the telephone
prompt: A Scottish-born inventor files a patent for a device that transmits the human voice over electrical wires — just hours before a rival inventor files a similar application.
hint: Alexander Graham Bell's first words over the telephone to his assistant Thomas Watson were reportedly: 'Mr. Watson, come here — I want to see you.'
epilogue: As Bell wired voices across America, the Battle of Little Bighorn saw Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse defeat Custer's 7th Cavalry, and the Meiji government was modernising Japan at extraordinary speed.

title: Edison demonstrates the electric light bulb
prompt: After testing over 6,000 materials for a filament, an American inventor holds a public demonstration of a long-lasting incandescent light bulb, keeping it glowing for over 13 hours.
hint: Edison didn't invent the idea of electric light — he invented the first practical, long-lasting version and the entire electrical infrastructure system to power it.
epilogue: As Edison illuminated Menlo Park in New Jersey, Zulu resistance to British rule was ending at the Battle of Ulundi in South Africa, and the first telephone exchange opened in London.

title: Berlin Conference — Africa divided
prompt: Fourteen European nations meet in Berlin to divide the African continent among themselves, drawing borders without consulting a single African.
hint: European powers divide a continent they barely know at a single Berlin meeting.
epilogue: Karl Benz was patenting the first automobile; the Statue of Liberty was under construction.

title: Benz builds the first petrol automobile
prompt: A German engineer builds a three-wheeled vehicle powered by an internal combustion engine — filing the patent for what is widely recognised as the world's first true automobile.
hint: Karl Benz's wife Bertha secretly took the car on an 104km trip without his knowledge, proving it worked and inventing the roadside repair stop along the way.
epilogue: As Benz invented the automobile in Mannheim, the Berlin Conference was dividing Africa among European powers, and the Statue of Liberty was being assembled in New York Harbour.

title: New Zealand grants women the vote
prompt: A self-governing British colony in the South Pacific becomes the first country in the world where women can vote in national elections.
hint: A Pacific nation becomes the first in the world to grant women's suffrage.
epilogue: The world was in a financial panic; the Ottoman Empire was entering its last decades.

title: Röntgen discovers X-rays
prompt: A German physicist accidentally discovers a new kind of ray that passes through flesh but not bone — he photographs his wife's hand, showing her skeleton, and she says: 'I have seen my own death.'
hint: He named them X-rays because he didn't know what they were. He won the first ever Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.
epilogue: As Röntgen made the invisible visible in Würzburg, the Lumière brothers invented cinema in Paris, and the Sino-Japanese War ended with Japan seizing Taiwan.

title: Marconi demonstrates wireless radio
prompt: A 21-year-old Italian inventor transmits a Morse code signal wirelessly across his father's estate — the first successful demonstration of radio communication.
hint: When the Italian government showed no interest, Marconi moved to England where the Post Office funded his research. He transmitted the first transatlantic radio signal in 1901.
epilogue: As Marconi beamed signals through the air in Bologna, the Dreyfus Affair was tearing France apart, and the Sino-Japanese War ended with Japan's emergence as a major power.

title: Ethiopia defeats Italy at Adwa
prompt: An Ethiopian emperor's army routs a colonial Italian force attempting to establish a protectorate, making Ethiopia the only African nation to successfully repel European colonisation.
hint: An African army routs a European colonial force, making one nation a symbol of resistance.
epilogue: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens the same year; gold was bringing fortune-seekers to South Africa.

title: Spanish-American War
prompt: An explosion on a US warship in Havana Harbour becomes the pretext for a war that transfers Spain's last colonies and makes America a global power.
hint: The USS Maine explosion in Cuba starts a war that ends the Spanish Empire.
epilogue: The Philippines, Puerto Rico, and Guam changed flags; Zionism was just being organised.

title: Philippine Revolution
prompt: Filipinos declare independence from Spain, but the US purchases the islands from Spain and begins its own colonial occupation.
hint: Filipinos win independence from Spain only to be sold to the United States.
epilogue: Marie Curie was discovering polonium; the Boer War was beginning in South Africa.

title: Marie Curie discovers radium
prompt: A Polish-born scientist working in a leaky Paris shed discovers two new radioactive elements, coins the term 'radioactivity', and becomes the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
hint: She won Nobel Prizes in both Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911) — the only person ever to win in two different sciences.
epilogue: As Curie isolated radium in Paris, the Spanish-American War was reshaping the Pacific and Caribbean, and the Boxer Rebellion was brewing in China.

title: Wright Brothers' first flight
prompt: Two bicycle-shop brothers from Ohio achieve the first controlled powered flight on a North Carolina beach.
hint: A wooden biplane leaves the sand at Kitty Hawk.
epilogue: The Russo-Japanese War would break out within a year; Einstein was about to publish special relativity.

title: Russian Revolution of 1905
prompt: After defeat by Japan, soldiers massacre peaceful protesters on Palace Square, triggering a revolution the Tsar barely survives.
hint: Troops fire on unarmed petitioners in St Petersburg on Bloody Sunday.
epilogue: Einstein published special relativity and four other landmark papers that same year.

title: Einstein's miracle year
prompt: A 26-year-old patent clerk in Bern publishes four papers that upend classical physics, including special relativity and the equivalence of mass and energy.
hint: A young physicist working in a Swiss patent office publishes E=mc² and rewrites the laws of physics.
epilogue: The Russian Revolution of 1905 was breaking out; the Wright Brothers had just flown two years earlier.

title: Fall of the Qing Dynasty
prompt: A republican revolution ends two thousand years of imperial rule in China; the last emperor is a five-year-old child.
hint: A revolution ends imperial China; a republic is proclaimed.
epilogue: The Titanic sank the following year; the Balkan Wars were about to begin.

title: Rutherford discovers the atomic nucleus
prompt: A New Zealand physicist fires alpha particles at gold foil — most pass through, but a few bounce straight back, as if they'd hit something tiny and incredibly dense at the atom's centre.
hint: He said it was like firing artillery shells at tissue paper and having them bounce back and hit you. This experiment revealed the nuclear model of the atom.
epilogue: As Rutherford mapped the atom in Manchester, the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire killed 146 workers in New York, and the Chinese Revolution overthrew the Qing dynasty.

title: Wegener proposes continental drift
prompt: A German meteorologist suggests that the continents were once one giant landmass that broke apart and drifted to their current positions — and is widely mocked by the scientific establishment.
hint: He noticed the coastlines of South America and Africa fit together like puzzle pieces, and found matching fossils on opposite sides of the Atlantic.
epilogue: As Wegener reshaped understanding of Earth itself, the Titanic sank on its maiden voyage, and the Balkan Wars were beginning to destabilise the Ottoman Empire.

title: Ford's moving assembly line transforms industry
prompt: An American carmaker introduces a conveyor belt assembly line in Detroit, slashing the time to build a car from 12 hours to 93 minutes — and making the automobile affordable to ordinary workers.
hint: Ford also doubled workers' wages to $5 a day, reasoning that his workers should be able to afford the products they made.
epilogue: While Ford revolutionised manufacturing in Detroit, the Balkan Wars were reshaping south-east Europe, and Mahatma Gandhi was leading his first major civil disobedience campaign in South Africa.

title: World War I begins
prompt: An assassin's bullet in Sarajevo ignites a chain of alliances and ultimatums that plunges the world into war.
hint: Austria declares war after an archduke is assassinated in Bosnia.
epilogue: The Panama Canal opened the same month; the Ottoman Empire was entering its last years.

title: Russian Revolution
prompt: Bolsheviks seize Petrograd and push Russia out of the war and into socialism.
hint: A red revolution topples the Russian Empire.
epilogue: America had just entered the Great War; the British were taking Baghdad and Jerusalem.

title: World War I ends
prompt: At the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month, guns fall silent across Europe after four years of industrial slaughter.
hint: An armistice signed in a railway carriage ends the Great War.
epilogue: The Spanish flu was killing more people than the war; the Ottoman Empire was collapsing.

title: British women win the vote
prompt: After decades of campaigning and wartime contributions, women over 30 gain the right to vote in British parliamentary elections for the first time.
hint: After chaining themselves to railings and enduring prison, British suffragettes win partial voting rights.
epilogue: Germany's armistice ended the Great War the same year; the Spanish flu was killing millions worldwide.

title: Turkish War of Independence
prompt: Mustafa Kemal leads a nationalist resistance that defeats Greek, French, and Armenian forces and establishes Turkey's modern borders.
hint: A general defeats multiple armies to carve out Turkey from Ottoman ruins.
epilogue: The League of Nations was meeting for the first time; Prohibition began in the United States.

title: Turkish Republic founded
prompt: From the ruins of the Ottoman Empire, a general-turned-statesman abolishes the sultanate and proclaims a modern secular republic.
hint: A victorious general abolishes the sultanate and founds a secular republic from Ottoman ruins.
epilogue: Mussolini marched on Rome the same year; the Soviet Union was forming.

title: Baird demonstrates television
prompt: A Scottish inventor gives the first public demonstration of a working television system to members of the Royal Institution in London — showing moving images of a ventriloquist's dummy.
hint: Baird's early television worked mechanically using spinning discs, not electronics. He also demonstrated colour TV, 3D TV, and even TV transmitted by radio wave — decades before anyone else.
epilogue: As Baird transmitted moving images in London, the General Strike paralysed Britain, and Hirohito ascended the Chrysanthemum Throne in Tokyo.

title: Lemaître proposes the Big Bang
prompt: A Belgian priest and physicist suggests that if the universe is expanding, winding it back in time leads to a single, inconceivably dense point — the origin of everything.
hint: Einstein initially told him his physics was correct but his astronomy was 'abominable.' Lemaître was vindicated when Hubble confirmed the universe was expanding.
epilogue: While Lemaître theorised the birth of the universe in Leuven, Charles Lindbergh crossed the Atlantic solo, and Chiang Kai-shek unified China under the Nationalist government.

title: Fleming discovers penicillin
prompt: A Scottish bacteriologist notices that a mould contaminating a petri dish kills surrounding bacteria, accidentally discovering the world's first antibiotic.
hint: A bacteriologist's contaminated petri dish accidentally yields the first antibiotic.
epilogue: The Wall Street Crash was a year away; Stalin was consolidating power through collectivisation.

title: Wall Street Crash
prompt: Stock markets in New York collapse over a few October days, ushering in the Great Depression.
hint: American stock prices collapse over Black Thursday and Tuesday.
epilogue: Stalin was consolidating power in the USSR; Gandhi was preparing the Salt March.

title: Hitler becomes Chancellor
prompt: A failed artist and veteran of the trenches is appointed head of government in Germany through legal means.
hint: A nationalist party leader takes power in Germany through the ballot box.
epilogue: Roosevelt's New Deal launched the same year; Japan had just invaded Manchuria.

title: Nuclear fission is discovered
prompt: Two German chemists bombard uranium with neutrons and find that the atom splits, releasing enormous energy — a discovery immediately recognised as the key to both nuclear power and atomic weapons.
hint: Lise Meitner, who fled Nazi Germany, helped interpret the results. She was later described by Einstein as 'the German Marie Curie.'
epilogue: As Hahn and Strassmann split the atom in Berlin, Kristallnacht had just shattered Jewish businesses across Germany, and in China the Nanjing Massacre was ongoing.

title: World War II begins
prompt: Germany invades Poland from the west and the Soviet Union from the east within weeks; Europe plunges back to war.
hint: Tanks roll into Poland from two directions; a second world war begins.
epilogue: The Spanish Civil War had just ended; DNA had not yet been mapped.

title: D-Day landings in Normandy
prompt: The largest amphibious invasion in history puts Allied troops on French beaches in a dawn assault.
hint: Allied forces storm beaches in northern France in the largest sea invasion ever mounted.
epilogue: The same year, the Bretton Woods system created the IMF and World Bank.

title: End of World War II
prompt: Two atomic bombs, Soviet entry into the Pacific war, and a surrender ceremony aboard a battleship in Tokyo Bay end the largest conflict in human history.
hint: Atomic weapons and a surrender ceremony end the greatest war in history.
epilogue: The United Nations was founded that same year; Indonesia and Vietnam declared independence.

title: United Nations founded
prompt: Delegates from 50 nations gather in a California city and sign a charter establishing a new international body pledged to prevent future wars.
hint: Representatives of 50 nations sign a charter in San Francisco pledging to prevent future conflicts.
epilogue: The atomic bombs had just fallen on Japan; Indonesia and Vietnam were declaring independence.

title: Indian National Army trials
prompt: Britain puts three officers of Subhas Chandra Bose's INA on trial for treason, and the resulting public outcry accelerates the independence movement.
hint: Treason trials backfire, turning captured soldiers into independence heroes.
epilogue: Japan had just surrendered; the United Nations charter was being signed in San Francisco.

title: ENIAC — the first general-purpose computer — completed
prompt: An 18-metre-long machine filled with 18,000 vacuum tubes is completed at the University of Pennsylvania — capable of performing thousands of calculations per second, programmed by teams of women mathematicians.
hint: The six women who programmed ENIAC — including Jean Jennings and Frances Bilas — were called 'computers' but went largely unrecognised for decades.
epilogue: As ENIAC was assembled in Philadelphia, World War II had just ended, the United Nations was being founded, and atomic bombs had been dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

title: Indian Independence and Partition
prompt: British India is partitioned at midnight into two new nations amid one of history's largest migrations.
hint: At midnight, British India becomes two new nations in a violent partition.
epilogue: The state of Israel would be proclaimed the next year; the Cold War was settling in.

title: The transistor is invented
prompt: Three physicists at Bell Laboratories in New Jersey create a tiny device that amplifies electrical signals — replacing the bulky vacuum tube and making modern electronics possible.
hint: The transistor is the most manufactured object in human history — over 10 sextillion (10²²) have been made. Your phone contains billions.
epilogue: As Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley invented the transistor in New Jersey, the Indian subcontinent was freshly partitioned into India and Pakistan, and the Marshall Plan was rebuilding post-war Europe.

title: First Arab-Israeli War
prompt: Hours after Israel declares independence, five Arab armies invade; the conflict creates hundreds of thousands of refugees on all sides.
hint: Israel declares independence and immediately faces invasion from neighbouring states.
epilogue: Gandhi had been assassinated months earlier; the Marshall Plan was rebuilding Europe.

title: People's Republic of China founded
prompt: Mao proclaims a new republic from the Gate of Heavenly Peace after decades of civil war.
hint: Mao proclaims a people's republic in Beijing after a long civil war.
epilogue: NATO was founded the same year; West and East Germany had just been formed.

title: Korean War begins
prompt: North Korean forces cross the 38th parallel in a surprise dawn attack, drawing in US and eventually Chinese forces.
hint: A surprise invasion across a parallel line divides a peninsula for generations.
epilogue: McCarthy's communist hunts were beginning in the US; NATO had just formed.

title: Egyptian Revolution
prompt: Army officers overthrow the king in a bloodless coup, ending British-backed monarchy and launching Arab nationalism.
hint: Egyptian officers topple a king and plant the seeds of Arab nationalism.
epilogue: The Korean War was still raging; Elizabeth II was crowned the following year.

title: Watson and Crick describe DNA
prompt: Two researchers at Cambridge, building on X-ray images taken by a colleague, determine that the molecule carrying genetic information is shaped like a twisted ladder.
hint: Two scientists use X-ray images to reveal that our genetic blueprint is a double helix.
epilogue: Stalin died the same year; the Korean War armistice was signed.

title: DNA double helix structure revealed
prompt: Two researchers at Cambridge use X-ray crystallography data, partly without permission, to deduce the double-helix structure of DNA — unlocking the mechanism of heredity.
hint: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray image, Photo 51, was the crucial data. She was not credited in the original paper and died before the Nobel Prize was awarded.
epilogue: As Watson and Crick decoded life's blueprint in Cambridge, Stalin died in Moscow ending an era of Soviet terror, and the Korean War armistice was being negotiated.

title: Brown v. Board of Education
prompt: The US Supreme Court unanimously rules that racial segregation in public schools is unconstitutional, overturning a 58-year-old precedent.
hint: The US Supreme Court rules that separate schools for Black and white children are unconstitutional.
epilogue: The Algerian War for independence was beginning; the French were losing at Dien Bien Phu.

title: Montgomery Bus Boycott
prompt: After a seamstress refuses to give up her seat on a city bus, a city's Black residents walk to work for over a year.
hint: A woman's refusal to give up her seat sparks a year-long boycott.
epilogue: Disneyland opened the same week; Vietnam was being divided at the 17th parallel.

title: Suez Crisis
prompt: Egypt's president nationalises the canal; Britain, France, and Israel invade, but US pressure forces them to withdraw — ending the era of European colonial power.
hint: A canal nationalisation ends Britain and France's era as global powers.
epilogue: The Hungarian uprising was crushed by Soviet tanks the same month.

title: Sputnik launched
prompt: A beach-ball-sized satellite beeps from orbit, stunning the world and kicking off the Space Race.
hint: A small Soviet satellite becomes the first object to orbit the Earth.
epilogue: Ghana had just become the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence.

title: Cuban Revolution
prompt: Fidel Castro's guerrillas enter Havana; a US-allied dictator flees with suitcases of cash.
hint: A guerrilla army marches into Havana.
epilogue: Alaska and Hawaii had just become US states; the transistor radio was everywhere.

title: Year of Africa
prompt: Seventeen African nations gain independence in a single year, reshaping the United Nations and the map of the world.
hint: In a single year, seventeen African flags replace colonial ensigns.
epilogue: JFK was elected in the US; the first laser was demonstrated.

title: Berlin Wall built
prompt: East Germany builds a wall overnight, dividing a city and symbolising the Iron Curtain for a generation.
hint: A wall goes up overnight, dividing a German city in two.
epilogue: Yuri Gagarin had orbited the Earth that April; the Bay of Pigs fiasco happened the same year.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
prompt: US spy planes photograph Soviet missiles in Cuba; for thirteen days the world holds its breath.
hint: Nuclear missiles in the Caribbean bring the world to the brink.
epilogue: The first communications satellite launched the same year; Watson and Crick had just described DNA.

title: US combat troops enter Vietnam
prompt: Marines wade ashore as the US commits ground troops to a Southeast Asian civil war.
hint: The first American combat Marines land on a Vietnamese beach.
epilogue: The Beatles were at the height of Beatlemania; the Voting Rights Act passed the same year.

title: Cultural Revolution begins
prompt: Mao mobilises China's youth as Red Guards to destroy the 'Four Olds' and purge his political rivals.
hint: Chinese students are mobilised to destroy the old order and purge Mao's enemies.
epilogue: The US was escalating in Vietnam; England was winning the World Cup.

title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
prompt: Two American astronauts walk on the lunar surface while half a billion people watch on television.
hint: A space agency in Florida fulfils a decade-old promise.
epilogue: That summer, half a million attended Woodstock; the ARPANET went live; Gaddafi took power in Libya.

title: ARPANET sends its first message
prompt: A computer at UCLA attempts to send the word 'LOGIN' to a computer at Stanford — the system crashes after the first two letters. The message received is 'LO.' The internet has begun.
hint: The network was designed to survive a nuclear attack by routing data around damaged nodes. Its creators had no idea it would one day connect billions of people.
epilogue: As ARPANET crept online in California, Neil Armstrong walked on the Moon, and Woodstock drew half a million people to a farm in upstate New York.

title: Intel releases the first commercial microprocessor
prompt: A Silicon Valley chip company releases a processor the size of a fingernail that contains all the computing power of a room-filling 1950s computer — originally designed for a Japanese calculator.
hint: The Intel 4004 had 2,300 transistors and ran at 740 kHz. A modern smartphone processor has over 15 billion transistors.
epilogue: As Intel's chip shrank computing to fingernail-size, Bangladesh won independence from Pakistan in a brutal war, and the decimalisation of British currency was completed.

title: Atari releases Pong
prompt: A startup company releases a coin-operated electronic tennis game in a bar in Sunnyvale, California — the machine breaks down within days because the coin box is overflowing with quarters.
hint: Atari co-founder Nolan Bushnell gave engineer Al Alcorn a simple challenge: build the tennis game as a learning exercise. Alcorn made it so good they released it as a product.
epilogue: As Pong revolutionised entertainment in California, Nixon visited China in a historic diplomatic thaw, and the Munich Olympics ended in tragedy when Palestinian militants killed Israeli athletes.

title: Yom Kippur War
prompt: Egypt and Syria launch a surprise attack on Israel on the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, reshaping Middle Eastern politics.
hint: Egypt and Syria attack Israel on a sacred fast day, triggering an oil embargo.
epilogue: The oil shock sent the world into recession; Pinochet's coup happened the same year.

title: Fall of Saigon
prompt: North Vietnamese tanks roll into the South Vietnamese capital as US helicopters evacuate the last Americans from a rooftop.
hint: Helicopter evacuations from a rooftop mark America's exit from Southeast Asia.
epilogue: The Khmer Rouge seized Cambodia the same week; Portugal's empire was collapsing.

title: First MRI scan of a human body
prompt: A physician straps himself into a machine and waits four hours while magnetic fields map the inside of his body — producing the first MRI image of a living human.
hint: Raymond Damadian filed the first MRI patent in 1972. The machine he built was called 'Indomitable.' Modern MRI scans take minutes rather than hours.
epilogue: While Damadian scanned human anatomy in New York, the first Star Wars film premiered in cinemas, and Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak had just launched Apple Computer.

title: Atari 2600 launches the home console era
prompt: A consumer electronics company releases a games console that uses interchangeable cartridges, allowing players to own multiple games — beginning the model that would define the games industry for decades.
hint: Originally called the Atari VCS (Video Computer System), it was renamed the 2600 when Atari released its successor. The port of Space Invaders sold 4x more units than the original arcade.
epilogue: As the Atari 2600 brought gaming into living rooms, the first Star Wars film premiered globally, Apple Computer was incorporated, and Deng Xiaoping was beginning China's economic reforms.

title: China's Reform and Opening Up
prompt: A pragmatic leader launches market reforms that will grow China into the world's second-largest economy within a generation.
hint: China's new leader opens the economy to markets and foreign investment.
epilogue: The Camp David Accords brought Egypt and Israel together the same year.

title: Space Invaders becomes Japan's first gaming phenomenon
prompt: An arcade game featuring waves of descending alien attackers becomes so popular in Japan that it causes a nationwide shortage of 100-yen coins, prompting the mint to quadruple production.
hint: Taito designer Tomohiro Nishikado had to build his own custom hardware because existing chips weren't powerful enough to move all the aliens. As aliens died, the survivors moved faster.
epilogue: As Space Invaders swept Japan, Egypt and Israel signed the Camp David Accords brokered by Jimmy Carter, and the first test-tube baby, Louise Brown, was born in England.

title: Iranian Revolution
prompt: A mass revolution overthrows the Shah; a cleric returns from exile to establish the world's first modern Islamic republic.
hint: A shah flees and a cleric returns from exile to found an Islamic republic.
epilogue: The Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan the same year; Margaret Thatcher became British PM.

title: Iran-Iraq War begins
prompt: Iraq invades Iran, starting an eight-year war that kills a million people and reshapes the Middle East.
hint: Iraq invades its neighbour one year after the Islamic Revolution.
epilogue: Reagan was elected US president; the Solidarity movement rose in Poland.

title: CNN launches as the first 24-hour news network
prompt: A flamboyant media mogul launches a cable television channel that broadcasts news around the clock — ridiculed as the 'Chicken Noodle Network' by competitors who thought no one wanted news all day.
hint: Ted Turner said at the launch: 'We won't be signing off until the world ends.' CNN went on to define how the world experienced events like the Gulf War live on television.
epilogue: As CNN debuted in Atlanta, the Iran-Iraq War began, Ronald Reagan was elected US president, and the Soviet Union was bogged down in Afghanistan.

title: Pac-Man becomes the world's first gaming icon
prompt: A Namco designer creates a maze game inspired by the shape of a pizza with a slice missing — deliberately designed to appeal to women and non-gamers, making it the first cultural crossover video game.
hint: Creator Toru Iwatani wanted to create a game that women would enjoy, in contrast to the shooting games of the era. Pac-Man became the best-selling arcade game of all time.
epilogue: As Pac-Man munched his way across arcades worldwide, the Iran hostage crisis was ongoing, Polish workers were striking to form Solidarity, and the Iran-Iraq War had just begun.

title: Tetris is created in Soviet Russia
prompt: A Soviet computer engineer at a Moscow research institute creates a simple puzzle game on a government computer — a game that can never be won, only delayed, that will become one of the best-selling games ever made.
hint: Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris on a Soviet Electronika 60 mainframe. He received no royalties for years because the Soviet government owned the rights.
epilogue: As Pajitnov built his falling blocks in Moscow, the miners' strike paralysed Britain, Indira Gandhi was assassinated in India, and Apple released the Macintosh computer.

title: Gorbachev launches Glasnost
prompt: A new Soviet leader introduces openness and restructuring policies that unleash forces he cannot control.
hint: A Soviet reformer's policies of openness and restructuring begin unravelling the USSR.
epilogue: Live Aid raised money for Ethiopian famine the same year; DNA fingerprinting was invented.

title: Nintendo Entertainment System launches in North America
prompt: A Japanese toy company revives a video game industry that had collapsed two years earlier by bundling its console with a toy robot, convincing sceptical retailers it was a toy, not a failed game machine.
hint: After the 1983 video game crash, US retailers refused to stock consoles. Nintendo disguised the NES as a toy, called it a 'Control Deck', and bundled it with R.O.B. the robot to get shelf space.
epilogue: As Nintendo revived gaming in New York, Live Aid raised $125 million for Ethiopian famine relief, Mikhail Gorbachev became Soviet leader, and the first .com domain was registered.

title: Super Mario Bros defines the platform game
prompt: A Japanese game designer who studied architecture creates a side-scrolling game where a plumber jumps on mushrooms and rescues a princess — introducing the most recognisable character in gaming history.
hint: Shigeru Miyamoto designed Mario as a universal, non-violent character to appeal across cultures. Mario's moustache, cap, and overalls were chosen to avoid drawing a mouth, hair, or shirt collar.
epilogue: While Mario jumped across Mushroom Kingdom, the internet's domain name system went live, Coca-Cola disastrously changed its formula, and the hole in the Antarctic ozone layer was confirmed.

title: Berlin Wall falls
prompt: East German guards, confused by a garbled press conference, open the checkpoints; Berliners dance on top of the wall.
hint: East Berliners walk freely through a wall for the first time in 28 years.
epilogue: The World Wide Web had just been proposed; Tiananmen Square had erupted months earlier.

title: Tim Berners-Lee invents the World Wide Web
prompt: A British scientist at a particle physics laboratory in Switzerland writes a proposal for an information-sharing system — his boss writes 'Vague but exciting' on the cover.
hint: Berners-Lee invented the Web to help physicists share research. He deliberately did not patent it, choosing to make it free to the world.
epilogue: As Berners-Lee sketched the Web in Geneva, the Berlin Wall fell, the Tiananmen Square protests were crushed in Beijing, and the Cold War was drawing to its close.

title: Nintendo Game Boy launches handheld gaming
prompt: Nintendo releases a portable games console with a tiny green-tinted screen powered by four AA batteries — beaten in every technical spec by rivals, yet it outsells them all combined.
hint: The Game Boy launched with Tetris bundled — a decision made by Nintendo's marketing chief Minoru Arakawa against the wishes of engineers. The pairing made both products unstoppable.
epilogue: As the Game Boy launched in Tokyo, the Berlin Wall fell, Tiananmen Square was crushed, and Tim Berners-Lee was sketching the World Wide Web at CERN.

title: Iraq invades Kuwait
prompt: Iraqi tanks roll across the Kuwaiti border overnight, triggering a US-led coalition to expel them.
hint: A midnight invasion of a small Gulf neighbour triggers a US-led war.
epilogue: Nelson Mandela was freed the same year; Germany was reunifying.

title: Hubble Space Telescope launched
prompt: NASA places a telescope above Earth's atmosphere, expecting crystal-clear images of the universe — but discovers the mirror is ground to the wrong shape, requiring a spacewalk repair mission three years later.
hint: Despite its flawed start, Hubble produced the famous Deep Field image showing thousands of galaxies in a patch of sky that appeared empty to the naked eye.
epilogue: As Hubble was launched into orbit, Nelson Mandela was freed from prison after 27 years, and German reunification was imminent following the fall of the Berlin Wall.

title: Soviet Union dissolves
prompt: Flags come down, a hammer and sickle descends from the Kremlin, and fifteen new republics are born.
hint: The USSR formally dissolves into fifteen republics.
epilogue: The first Gulf War had just ended; Linux was released that year.

title: Doom launches the first-person shooter genre
prompt: Two developers in Dallas distribute a fast, violent three-dimensional shooting game over the internet as shareware — it becomes so popular it crashes university networks and attracts 10 million downloads.
hint: id Software's John Carmack pioneered the 3D rendering engine that made Doom possible. The game was so widespread that shareware Doom was estimated to be installed on more computers than Windows 95.
epilogue: As Doom stormed onto PCs, the Oslo Accords brought hope of Middle East peace, Nelson Mandela and F.W. de Klerk shared the Nobel Peace Prize, and the Mosaic web browser made the internet visual.

title: Mandela elected president
prompt: South Africa holds its first fully democratic election and elects a man just released from 27 years in prison.
hint: South Africa ends apartheid with a historic election.
epilogue: Rwanda's genocide was unfolding; NAFTA had just taken effect.

title: Rwandan Genocide
prompt: In one hundred days, an estimated 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu are killed by extremists, in one of history's fastest and most concentrated acts of mass murder.
hint: A hundred-day campaign of mass killing in Central Africa horrifies the world.
epilogue: The Channel Tunnel opened that year; Nelson Mandela was being inaugurated in South Africa.

title: Sony PlayStation launches
prompt: An electronics giant enters the video game market with a CD-based console after a deal with Nintendo collapsed — it goes on to become the best-selling console of its generation and Sony's most profitable product ever.
hint: The PlayStation originated from a CD-ROM add-on Sony was developing for the SNES. When Nintendo cancelled the deal, Sony's Ken Kutaragi convinced the company to build its own console instead.
epilogue: As Sony's PlayStation launched in Tokyo, Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as South Africa's first Black president, the Channel Tunnel opened between England and France, and the Rwandan genocide killed 800,000 people.

title: Dolly the sheep is cloned
prompt: Scientists in Edinburgh announce the birth of a lamb that was not created by sexual reproduction — she was cloned from a single cell of an adult sheep's mammary gland.
hint: Dolly was named after Dolly Parton because she was cloned from a mammary cell. She lived for 6 years and was later stuffed and put in a museum.
epilogue: As Dolly was born in Edinburgh, the Taliban seized control of Kabul, and China's handover of Hong Kong from Britain was only a year away.

title: Pokémon Red and Green launch in Japan
prompt: A Game Boy game about catching creatures in tall grass sells out immediately in Japan — and becomes the best-selling role-playing series in history, spawning the highest-grossing media franchise ever.
hint: Designer Satoshi Tajiri was inspired by his childhood hobby of collecting insects. He spent six years developing the game, nearly bankrupting his studio multiple times.
epilogue: As Pikachu and friends debuted in Tokyo, the Atlanta Olympics featured 197 nations and a bombing in Centennial Park, Dolly the sheep was cloned in Edinburgh, and the Taliban seized Kabul.

title: Nintendo 64 launches with 3D gaming
prompt: Nintendo releases a 64-bit console with a revolutionary three-pronged controller — launching alongside a game that defined 3D gaming so completely that it is still considered the greatest game ever made.
hint: The N64's launch title was Super Mario 64, which established the conventions of 3D platform games. Ocarina of Time followed two years later, setting the template for 3D adventure games still used today.
epilogue: As Nintendo took gaming into three dimensions, Dolly the sheep became the first cloned mammal in Edinburgh, the Atlanta Olympics were overshadowed by a bombing, and Tupac Shakur was shot in Las Vegas.

title: Hong Kong handed to China
prompt: Britain hands its last major colony to China in a midnight ceremony, ending 156 years of colonial rule.
hint: A midnight handover ceremony returns a great port city to China.
epilogue: The Kyoto Protocol was signed; Princess Diana died in a Paris tunnel.

title: September 11 attacks
prompt: Hijacked planes strike the Twin Towers and the Pentagon; the post-Cold War era ends within an hour.
hint: Four hijacked planes reshape American foreign policy in a single morning.
epilogue: Wikipedia launched that year; Apple released the first iPod.

title: Microsoft launches the Xbox
prompt: The world's largest software company enters the console hardware market with a machine built like a PC — launching alongside a game where a super-soldier fights aliens on a ring-shaped mega-structure.
hint: Halo: Combat Evolved was specifically designed to launch with the Xbox and establish it as a serious gaming platform. The Xbox also introduced broadband online gaming to consoles via Xbox Live.
epilogue: As Microsoft launched its gaming ambitions, the September 11 attacks reshaped global politics, the iPod launched a revolution in portable music, and Afghanistan fell to US-led coalition forces.

title: Invasion of Iraq
prompt: A US-led coalition invades Iraq without UN approval, toppling a dictator but unleashing years of insurgency.
hint: Coalition forces topple a statue of a dictator in Baghdad.
epilogue: The Human Genome Project was completed the same year; SARS emerged in China.

title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
prompt: A 9.1-magnitude earthquake off Sumatra generates waves that kill over 200,000 people across fourteen countries.
hint: An undersea earthquake off Indonesia sends deadly waves across three oceans.
epilogue: Facebook was founded weeks later; the Athens Olympics had just concluded.

title: World of Warcraft launches the MMO era
prompt: An online game set in a fantasy world with no ending launches and attracts 1 million subscribers within a month — peaking at 12 million players and creating the template for the massively multiplayer online genre.
hint: WoW's monthly subscription model generated over $9 billion in revenue at its peak. The game had its own functioning economy, social rituals, and even sparked a study by US epidemiologists modelling disease spread.
epilogue: As millions entered Azeroth, Facebook launched from a Harvard dorm room, the Indian Ocean tsunami killed 230,000 people, and the European Union expanded to 25 member states.

title: Nintendo Wii brings motion controls to living rooms
prompt: Nintendo releases a console that uses a motion-sensing remote to detect arm movements — bringing grandparents and non-gamers into gaming, and outselling its more powerful competitors by selling 100 million units.
hint: Nintendo's strategy was to expand the market rather than compete on hardware power. Wii Sports, bundled with the console, became the second best-selling game ever and caused a global supply shortage.
epilogue: As Wii made everyone a gamer, Twitter launched with its first tweet, Saddam Hussein was executed in Baghdad, and Pluto was controversially reclassified as a dwarf planet.

title: Apple launches the iPhone
prompt: A tech company unveils a touchscreen phone with no physical keyboard, combining a mobile phone, an iPod, and an internet browser — a product its CEO calls 'revolutionary.'
hint: Steve Jobs announced it by saying Apple was introducing three revolutionary products: a widescreen iPod, a mobile phone, and an internet communicator. Then revealed it was all one device.
epilogue: As Jobs unveiled the iPhone in San Francisco, the Iraq War entered its fifth year, China hosted its first Formula One Grand Prix, and the global financial crisis was quietly brewing.

title: Global Financial Crisis
prompt: A major American investment bank collapses, freezing credit markets worldwide and triggering the worst recession since the 1930s.
hint: Lehman Brothers collapses, triggering a global recession.
epilogue: Barack Obama was elected the same year; Bitcoin's whitepaper appeared.

title: Beijing Olympics
prompt: China opens the most expensive Olympic Games in history, announcing its arrival as a global power with a spectacular opening ceremony.
hint: An opening ceremony with 15,000 performers signals China's rise.
epilogue: The global financial crisis hit weeks after the closing ceremony.

title: Bitcoin is launched
prompt: An anonymous person (or group) using the name Satoshi Nakamoto releases software for a decentralised digital currency with no central bank — the first transaction buys 10,000 BTC worth of pizza years later.
hint: The true identity of Satoshi Nakamoto remains unknown. Over 1 million Bitcoin in the original wallet have never been moved.
epilogue: As Bitcoin emerged from the 2008 financial crisis, Barack Obama was inaugurated as the first Black US president, and the Large Hadron Collider at CERN was restarting after a setback.

title: Arab Spring
prompt: Mass protests topple Egypt's long-ruling president; a wave of uprisings sweeps the Arab world.
hint: Eighteen days of protests in Tahrir Square topple a 30-year ruler.
epilogue: Osama bin Laden was killed the same year; Japan suffered a devastating earthquake and tsunami.

title: Minecraft officially releases
prompt: A solo Swedish developer releases the full version of a blocky sandbox game he built as a side project — it becomes the best-selling video game of all time, with over 238 million copies sold.
hint: Markus 'Notch' Persson originally called it 'Cave Game' and coded the first prototype in six days. Microsoft bought Minecraft and Mojang for $2.5 billion in 2014.
epilogue: As Minecraft's world became the most built-in ever, the Arab Spring toppled governments from Tunisia to Libya, Japan's Fukushima disaster followed a devastating earthquake, and the last Space Shuttle flew.

title: Higgs boson discovered at CERN
prompt: Scientists at the world's largest particle accelerator announce they have found the last missing piece of the Standard Model of particle physics — the field that gives all matter its mass.
hint: The discovery confirmed a theory proposed in 1964 by Peter Higgs and five other physicists. The particle had been nicknamed 'the God particle' by the press.
epilogue: As CERN announced the Higgs boson, the Arab Spring revolutions were reshaping the Middle East, and SpaceX became the first private company to dock with the International Space Station.

title: CRISPR gene editing developed
prompt: Two scientists publish a paper describing a molecular tool that can cut and edit DNA with unprecedented precision — giving humanity the ability to rewrite the genetic code of any living organism.
hint: Based on a bacterial immune system, CRISPR-Cas9 works like molecular scissors. Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for it.
epilogue: As CRISPR gave scientists the power to edit life itself, civil war erupted in Syria, and the Mars rover Curiosity was making its first discoveries on the red planet.

title: Paris Climate Agreement
prompt: Representatives of 196 nations meet and sign the first universal agreement to limit global warming, pledging to keep temperature rise well below 2°C.
hint: Nearly every nation signs a landmark agreement in Paris pledging to limit the warming of the planet.
epilogue: The Syrian refugee crisis was at its height; China had just become the world's largest economy by some measures.

title: Nintendo Switch launches as hybrid console
prompt: Nintendo releases a console that docks to a TV at home but detaches into a handheld device — proving that a single concept that failed as pure tablet or pure console could succeed as both.
hint: The Switch launched with The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, widely considered the greatest game ever made. The console sold 140 million units — Nintendo's most successful hardware ever.
epilogue: As Nintendo redefined gaming hardware, Donald Trump was inaugurated as US president, the UK triggered Article 50 beginning Brexit, and Elon Musk's SpaceX successfully landed a reused rocket booster.

title: Fortnite becomes a global cultural phenomenon
prompt: A battle royale mode added almost as an afterthought to a zombie game within two weeks of a competitor's release becomes the most-played game in the world, with 350 million registered accounts.
hint: Epic Games added the Battle Royale mode after PUBG popularised the genre. Fortnite became famous for in-game concerts by Travis Scott and Ariana Grande watched by millions simultaneously.
epilogue: As Fortnite took over screens worldwide, the Rohingya crisis unfolded in Myanmar, Hurricane Maria devastated Puerto Rico, and the #MeToo movement began reshaping workplaces globally.

title: COVID-19 pandemic begins
prompt: A new coronavirus spreads from a central Chinese city, and within months the world locks down.
hint: A novel virus shuts down cities across the globe.
epilogue: George Floyd protests swept the United States; Brexit formally took effect.

title: PlayStation 5 launches during a global pandemic
prompt: Sony releases its next-generation console during lockdowns worldwide — immediately selling out everywhere, as homebound consumers snap up every unit available, making it the fastest-selling console in history.
hint: The PS5's solid-state drive reduced game loading times from minutes to seconds. The DualSense controller introduced haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that could simulate bowstrings, mud, and rain.
epilogue: As the PS5 launched amid COVID lockdowns, the US election saw record turnout, vaccines began rolling out across the world, and the Black Lives Matter movement had just reshaped global conversations on race.
